discovery: Prediction and experimental confirmation of anyons: particles with fractional exchange statistics in two dimensions

nominees.name: Jan Myrheim
nominees.affiliation: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), Trondheim, Norway

subfield: Condensed matter physics / topological quantum matter
motivation: In 1977 Leinaas and Myrheim showed, from a careful analysis of the configuration space of identical particles, that quantum mechanics in two dimensions permits exchange statistics interpolating continuously between bosons and fermions. This overturned a textbook assumption and founded the physics of anyons. The idea became central to the fractional quantum Hall effect, topological order and proposals for fault-tolerant topological quantum computation. For decades direct evidence was lacking. In 2020 Manfra and collaborators used Fabry-Perot interferometry in engineered GaAs heterostructures to observe the anyonic braiding phase of fractionally charged quasiparticles directly, and later experiments have extended this work. Taken together, the prediction and its confirmation show that a new kind of quantum statistics exists in nature. They have changed how physicists, and students, understand identical particles and quantum matter.
